work.title: The Preserving Machine and Other Stories

reading.synopsis: First published by Ace Books in 1969 and anchored by its title story -- in which a machine transforms musical compositions into living creatures in an attempt to preserve them against a feared future collapse of culture -- this collection showcases Dick's inventive short fiction from the 1950s and 1960s.
motifs: Art and culture rendered fragile, requiring extraordinary or fantastical intervention to survive an anticipated collapse
reading.significance: The title story's premise -- transforming Beethoven, Mozart, and Schubert into literal living animals to save them from an imagined coming dark age -- is a distinctive early expression of Dick's recurring concern with the fragility and endangerment of cultural and artistic value, later echoed in different registers throughout his career.
reading.closing_note: This entry documents the anthology as a publishing object; readers seeking analysis of the title story should consult its own dedicated dossier ('the-preserving-machine') elsewhere in this corpus.
